candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: apply medication knowledge to safe antimicrobial therapy, evaluate medication effectiveness, and support appropriate medication use.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — antimicrobial stewardship and carbapenem conservation
candidate.educational_objective: Apply antimicrobial stewardship by using infection site and susceptibility data to select an effective preferred agent and conserving carbapenems when narrower recommended therapy is active, rather than treating ESBL status alone as an automatic indication for meropenem.

options.A: Nitrofurantoin is a preferred option; although carbapenems can be effective, avoiding them when an effective narrower option is available helps preserve their activity for infections with fewer treatment choices.
options.B: Meropenem should be preferred whenever an ESBL-producing organism is identified, regardless of infection site or susceptibility to other recommended agents.
options.C: Carbapenems have no activity against ESBL-producing Enterobacterales, so meropenem susceptibility should be considered a laboratory error.
options.D: Once ESBL production is identified, antimicrobial susceptibility results no longer influence antibiotic selection.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current IDSA 2026 antimicrobial-resistance guidance lists nitrofurantoin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole as preferred options for uncomplicated cystitis caused by ESBL-producing Enterobacterales when active. Carbapenems can be effective alternatives, but their use is discouraged when an effective preferred option is available because limiting carbapenem use preserves their activity for future infections in which treatment options may be more restricted. B overgeneralizes carbapenem use without considering infection site and other susceptible agents. C is false because ESBL-producing Enterobacterales generally remain susceptible to carbapenems. D is incorrect because the IDSA guidance assumes in-vitro activity of selected agents and repeatedly uses susceptibility results to guide therapy.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For uncomplicated ESBL-E cystitis with nitrofurantoin susceptibility, nitrofurantoin is preferred and carbapenem use should generally be conserved; ESBL status does not replace infection-site and susceptibility-guided antimicrobial selection.
candidate.source_document_title: IDSA 2026 Guidance on the Treatment of Antimicrobial Resistant Gram-Negative Infections; Meropenem for Injection Prescribing Information
candidate.source_locator: IDSA 2026 AMR Guidance — Section 1, ESBL-producing Enterobacterales, Question 1.1: nitrofurantoin and TMP-SMX are preferred for uncomplicated ESBL-E cystitis; fluoroquinolones and carbapenems are effective alternatives but their use is discouraged when preferred agents are active because limiting them preserves activity for future infections. Section 1 introduction: ESBL-E generally remain susceptible to carbapenems and treatment suggestions assume in-vitro activity. DailyMed Meropenem — Section 1 Usage: use for infections proven or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria.

candidate.stem: A urine culture from a stable client with uncomplicated cystitis grows ESBL-producing Escherichia coli susceptible to both nitrofurantoin and meropenem. Which stewardship principle should the nurse recognize when reviewing the treatment plan?
